propositions: A transient GitHub git fetch hang during clone times out at _GIT_TIMEOUT=300s and raises SnapshotFetchError, which is caught by adapter.code_review_decision's blanket except and mapped to a spurious BLOCK decision with -1 vote

The -1 vote removes the change from backfill reconciliation permanently because reconcile.py pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote() and skips already-voted changes, preventing self-healing retry on the next pass

Infrastructure timeouts (git fetch, network connection stalls, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) should be distinguished from genuine review conclusions and routed to a no-vote abstain path instead of fail-closed voting

The fix adds _is_retryable_infra classifier to detect transient infrastructure faults and returns ABSTAIN decision, causing voter to emit VOTER_ERROR marker, post no vote, write no dedup row, and return status=abstained
An abstained change without a vote remains eligible for backfill reconciliation on the next pass, restoring the designed safety net for transient faults
